ledger.claim: The driver's own trace measures this trip at 12.4 km against a booked optimal of 7.5 km on the AYE eastbound — an excess of 4.9 km, which is 65.33% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are passed: the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED, and because the excess also exceeds 50% of optimal it is additionally a MATERIAL deviation. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (12.4 km), which the clause makes the field for the threshold test; here it coincides with the trip_record copy, so the test is safe on either reading.

No clause adjusts the excess downward on this record. There was no pickup or dropoff amendment on this trip — pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null — so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no re-quote reduces the measured distance. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 has no application either. The 4.9 km excess stands as measured.

The driver's account is that the rider asked for Clementi and that he drove the Clementi way. His own trace refutes the corroboration POL-RD-04 requires: the waypoint the platform resolved from the rider's chat message (waypoint_hint, The Clementi Mall) is never approached — the nearest fix on EV-GPS-00311 is 2,595.3 m away, at 16:08:45, against the 200 m threshold POL-RD-04 sets, and within_threshold is false. Under POL-RD-04 the waypoint_hint coordinate is the field the test uses and no party may geocode a place name instead; the test fails. POL-RD-14 then governs: a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent with each other, not the contradiction POL-RD-10(7) describes. No distance is excluded, no amended optimal is supplied, and the deviation stands at the measured figure.

The counterparty statement adds that the rider said 'never mind go straight' and invites the tribunal to 'check the chat'. The chat export is complete and untruncated and contains exactly two messages: the rider's request to stop at Clementi Mall at 16:06:05 and the driver's 'ok' at 16:06:35. There is no withdrawal message anywhere on the record. An assertion the citing party's own artifact does not support carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the uncorroborated instruction is disposed of under POL-RD-14.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes and the deviation may therefore rest on it alone. EV-GPS-00311 carries 145 fixes at a 10 second cadence across the whole active window with 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires on this trace. No independent corroboration is needed under POL-RD-07(ii), and the mandatory-escalation trigger in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00311-01, is MISSING: it has no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. I disclose that impairment expressly, and rely on the absence itself, which POL-GEN-02 makes citable. With no advisory covering this trip's window, POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and no external traffic cause — whatever either party asserts — can exonerate any part of the 4.9 km excess; under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The same trip identifier TRP-00311 and the same pickup event are carried on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, satisfying limb (a); and the excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold is measured from a trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), satisfying limb (b). The rider profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required under the rider-profile test and it could not be used to deny this claim in any event. The burden has shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12 — and not one of those routes survives on this record.

Because the deviation is MATERIAL (over 50% of optimal), POL-RD-06 requires the driver_profile check, and I state its result honestly: the check is run and no pattern is established. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 260 — below both the 3-flag test and the 0.05 ratio test — so no FULL_REFUND uplift under limb (b) and no conduct referral under limb (c) follow. The rider does not press for either. The rider's remedy is the POL-RD-02 recomputation on this trip's own evidence.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 fixes the money arithmetically rather than at the tribunal's discretion. Read from the fare_breakdown: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.5 + 0.28 x 12.0) x the surge_multiplier of 1.00 recorded on EV-FARE-00311 = 12.785, plus the 0.80 platform fee and zero ERP, tolls, surcharges, waiting time and promo = 13.585. charged_total is 20.62. Refund = 20.62 - 13.585 = 7.035, rounded up to a payable of SGD 7.05. That is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and it is 34.1% of charged_total, short of the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 7.05 — the rider asked for 5.00 and the arithmetic gives more.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern on this record and therefore no uplift. The driver's counters are 0 deviation flags in 90 days on 260 completed trips, so both limbs of POL-RD-06 fail: the flag count is far below 3, and the ratio is 0.00 against the 0.05 threshold with the 40-trip floor comfortably satisfied. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field, and POL-GEN-01 forbids reading it in place of the 90-day figure the clause names. With no pattern established, the balanced-evidence limb, the FULL_REFUND uplift and the driver-conduct referral are all unavailable, and the rider's demand for the fare back has nothing to stand on.

ledger.claim: Any refund on this trip is the POL-RD-02 recomputation and nothing further. Charged_total is 20.62; recomputed_fare is 13.5850 (3.80 base fare plus 0.75 x 7.5 km plus 0.28 x 12.0 min at the fare breakdown's own surge multiplier of 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, toll, surcharge or waiting-time line to add); the difference is 7.0350, footed up to 7.05 payable. That is 34.1% of the charge, well short of the 90% that would convert a partial into a FULL_REFUND, and above the 0.50 de minimis floor. The rider's request for the whole fare is out of reach, and the ruling should say so on separate lines as the clause requires.

Whatever the arithmetic produces, the award cannot exceed what was contested. POL-GEN-03 defines amount_sgd as the refund to the filing party, PARTIAL_REFUND as the return of part of the contested amount and FULL_REFUND as the return of the whole of it. The rider put SGD 5.00 in issue, so even taking the POL-RD-02 figure of 7.05 at its highest, the amount returned to her is capped at SGD 5.00.

Nothing is added on top of the distance-and-time figure, and there is no billing-integrity finding to make. The fare carries no ERP gantries, zero tolls and no airport surcharge (this trip ends at Buona Vista and does not originate at an airport), so the pass-through correction has nothing to correct; POL-RD-09(1) in any event bars adding off-route ERP on top of a POL-RD-02 refund; and because no charge line is unmatched by the trip record and trace, POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged and no referral is warranted.

The baseline is the booked optimal of 7.5 km from the routing engine, not the '7 km' the rider asserts from memory. POL-RD-01 takes the platform estimate stored on the trip record as the optimal distance, and no adjustment is available on this record: both amendment timestamps are null and no amended optimal is stored, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and there is nothing to move the baseline. Measured on the governing trace figure the excess is 4.9 km and 65.3%, and the rider's smaller estimate would only inflate it.

The rider's account of where the vehicle went is not in evidence. No venue_id in this bundle identifies any point as Bukit Timah, and nothing in the chat log says it either; under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID is discarded, and POL-RD-01 fixes the measure as the trace rather than the narrative. The driver can therefore be charged only with the trace's measured excess of 4.9 km, not with a loop whose geography no admitted artifact establishes.

The driver does not press rider-requested-detour exoneration under POL-RD-04, and the tribunal should not spend the case on it. The rider's message at 16:06:05 does name The Clementi Mall and the driver answered 'ok' at 16:06:35, but POL-RD-04 requires the trace to corroborate the instruction: the closest fix to the waypoint is 2,595.3 m against a 200 m threshold, so the corroboration fails and under POL-RD-14 no distance is excluded and the deviation is decided on the trace as measured. The driver's further account of a withdrawal - 'never mind go straight' - does not appear in the two-message export and he does not rely on it. What the chat log does show is that the rider herself asked to divert to Clementi within a minute of departure, which her claim that the driver looped 'for no reason' leaves out.

ruling.explanation:
Ruling on dispute DSP-00311 (trip TRP-00311). Both of you read the same records; here is what they show and how the money is fixed.

DEVIATION. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00311 (weight 1.0) measures the trip at 12.4 km, against the booked optimal of 7.5 km on the AYE (EV-TRIP-00311). The excess is 4.9 km — 65.3% of optimal — so both POL-RD-01 tests pass: the deviation is ESTABLISHED, and at over 50% it is additionally MATERIAL. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps), so it carries the finding on its own and POL-RD-07/POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged.

RIDER-REQUESTED STOP. The driver says the rider asked for Clementi. The chat log EV-CHAT-00311 does show her 16:06:05 request and his 'ok', but POL-RD-04 requires the trace to corroborate a rider instruction, and the nearest fix to the waypoint the platform resolved from that message (The Clementi Mall) is 2,595.3 m away against the 200 m threshold — the vehicle never approached it. Under POL-RD-14 the instruction therefore did not cause the excess: no distance is excluded and no amended optimal is supplied. The driver's further account of a 'never mind, go straight' message does not appear in the complete, untruncated two-message export, and he does not rely on it.

TRAFFIC. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00311-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0; issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no advisory on file covers this trip, POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and no external traffic cause exonerates any part of the excess (POL-RD-13). The deviation stands at the measured figure, and the finding does not rest on that absent artifact.

MONEY. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 fixes the refund arithmetically. Read from EV-FARE-00311: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 7.5 km + 0.28 x 12.0 min) x the fare breakdown's surge multiplier of 1.00, plus 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP, tolls, surcharges, waiting time and promo = 13.585. Charged_total is 20.62. Refund = 20.62 - 13.585 = 7.035, rounded up to SGD 7.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 34.1% of the charge — short of the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND — so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 7.05.

On the driver's point that the award cannot exceed the SGD 5.00 recorded as contested: POL-RD-02 measures the refund as charged_total less the recomputed fare and no clause caps it at the contested figure. The record supports a fare correction of SGD 7.05, and that is the amount awarded; the tribunal corrects the bill to the correct fare rather than to the figure the rider happened to name.

Nothing is added for ERP, tolls or surcharges — none was charged (0.00) — so POL-RD-09 produces no pass-through correction, there is no unmatched line, and no billing-integrity referral arises. The POL-RD-06 profile check was run as the MATERIAL finding requires (0 deviation flags in 90 days on 260 completed trips): no pattern is established, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. Driver compensation under POL-RD-04 is not available either: the distance billed (12.4 km) is not less than the trace records.

The monetary effect (SGD 7.05) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue. Every automated ruling is provisional; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
